page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor, running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is arm64, featuring one thread per core with dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps, all operating on the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark testing, the c8gd.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, ranking in the top 10% for both large block read and write operations. Multi-core performance is strong, with Geekbench multi-core and software compilation tests scoring in the top 10%. Database operations and static web serving throughput also reach top-tier levels. However, single-core performance, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, remains in the average tier. LLM inference speeds for small, medium, and large models also fall within the average range.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c8gd.12xlarge is driven by its high physical core density and ARMv9 architecture, which delivers strong multi-threaded throughput per resource unit. The inclusion of 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage reduces the need for external block storage, optimizing data-intensive workloads. A key tradeoff is the lower memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which may limit memory-bound applications, alongside average single-core performance.

This server is configured for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and local storage-dependent applications. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or single-threaded tasks.
